sections.heading: Climate change, international protocols & India's commitment

blocks.text: **Climate change** — long-term shifts in temperature and weather driven by **greenhouse-gas emissions** — is the defining environmental challenge. It is addressed globally through **UNFCCC protocols** and India's own ambitious **net-zero and NDC commitments**.

rows: Rio; parent framework; annual **CoP** meetings; principle of **CBDR**.
Binding emission cuts for developed nations.
**Net-zero by 2070; Panchamrit (Glasgow CoP26); Mission LiFE; updated NDCs**.

sections.heading: 🌿 Exam-ready deep coverage: climate change & protocols

items: **Cause**: greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, F-gases, water vapour) trap heat → global warming; **IPCC** (scientific body, AR6) warns of ~1.1°C warming already.

**Global regime**: **UNFCCC (Rio 1992)** → **Kyoto Protocol (1997)** (binding for developed nations; CDM) → **Paris Agreement (2015)** — limit warming to **well below 2°C, aim 1.5°C**, via **NDCs**, common-but-differentiated responsibilities (CBDR); **CoP** meetings (CoP28-UAE loss-and-damage fund).

**India's stand & pledges (Panchamrit, COP26)**: 500 GW non-fossil by 2030, 50% RE, cut 1 bn t emissions, reduce emissions intensity 45%, **Net-Zero by 2070**; **LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)**, ISA, CDRI.
**Mechanisms**: carbon markets/credits, green finance, adaptation & mitigation.

prelimsPointers: **UNFCCC (1992, Rio)** — parent treaty; principle of **Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR)**.
**Kyoto Protocol (1997)** — binding cuts for developed nations; **Paris Agreement (2015)** — NDC-based.
**Mission LiFE** (Lifestyle for Environment) — India's behavioural-change initiative.
India-led: **ISA, CDRI, LiFE**; CoP28 set up the **loss-and-damage fund**.

glossary.definition: The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (1992), the parent climate treaty.
The 2015 accord to limit warming below 2°C via nationally determined contributions.
Balancing greenhouse gases emitted and removed; India's target year is 2070.

blocks.text: India protects its **forests and wildlife** through dedicated laws and a network of **protected areas and species-conservation projects** — vital for biodiversity, climate and tribal livelihoods.

rows: Protects species; creates national parks & sanctuaries; schedules by protection level.
**National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves, Conservation/Community Reserves, Tiger Reserves**.
**Project Tiger (1973), Project Elephant, Project Lion, Cheetah reintroduction**.

sections.heading: 🌿 Exam-ready deep coverage: forest & wildlife conservation

items: **Forest cover**: ~24-25% (FSI **India State of Forest Report**, biennial); **National Forest Policy 1988** target = **33%**; classification — reserved/protected/unclassed.

**Laws**: **Forest Conservation Act 1980** (diversion needs central nod), **Wildlife Protection Act 1972** (Schedules I-IV; national parks/sanctuaries), **Forest Rights Act 2006** (tribal/OTFD rights), **CAMPA** (compensatory afforestation), Van (Sanrakshan) Adhiniyam 2023.
**Programmes**: **Project Tiger (1973 → NTCA, ~55 tiger reserves), Project Elephant, Project Lion, Project Dolphin, Project Cheetah (2022 — Kuno)**, Green India Mission, Nagar Van.
**Wetlands & Ramsar**: India has 80+ Ramsar sites (most in Asia); **Coringa/Kolleru (AP)**.

prelimsPointers: **Forest Rights Act, 2006** — rights of forest-dwelling tribes.
**Project Tiger (1973)** — India holds ~**70% of the world's wild tigers**; **NTCA** manages tiger reserves.
**Forest Conservation Act 1980, Wildlife Protection Act 1972, FRA 2006, CAMPA**.
**Project Tiger (1973) → NTCA**; **Project Cheetah (2022, Kuno)**; Project Elephant/Dolphin/Lion.
India has the **most Ramsar sites in Asia** (80+).

glossary.definition: India's principal law protecting wild species and creating protected areas.
The 1973 conservation programme that recovered India's tiger population.
The 2006 law recognising forest-dwelling communities' rights.

sections.heading: Environmental hazards, pollution, carbon emission & global warming

blocks.text: **Pollution** — the contamination of air, water, soil and noise — and rising **carbon emissions** drive **global warming and health hazards**. Understanding pollutants, their sources and controls is central to environmental science.

rows: **PM2.5/PM10, SO₂, NOₓ, CO, O₃**; measured by **AQI**; sources — vehicles, industry, stubble.
Sewage, industrial effluent, agrochemicals; indicators **BOD, COD**.
Rise in Earth's temperature from GHG-driven greenhouse effect.
Sea-level rise, extreme weather, glacial melt, health impacts.

sections.heading: 🌿 Exam-ready deep coverage: pollution & global warming

items: **Air pollution**: PM2.5/PM10, SO₂, NOₓ, CO, O₃; **AQI**; **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**; smog, stubble burning; **BS-VI** fuel norms.
**Water pollution**: sewage, industrial effluent, eutrophication; **Namami Gange**; groundwater contamination (arsenic, fluoride).
**Soil & solid waste**: plastic (Single-Use Plastic ban 2022, EPR), e-waste, hazardous waste rules; **Swachh Bharat**.
**Global warming impacts**: sea-level rise, extreme weather, glacial melt, agriculture & health effects; carbon footprint & carbon markets; ozone depletion (Montreal).
**Regulators**: CPCB/SPCB, NGT; AP Pollution Control Board (APPCB) — post-disaster monitoring (e.g., LG Polymers 2020).

prelimsPointers: Air pollutants — **PM2.5, PM10, SO₂, NOₓ, CO, ground-level ozone**; measured by the **Air Quality Index (AQI)**.
Greenhouse gases — **CO₂, methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide, CFCs**; **CO₂** the largest contributor.
**Global warming** = temperature rise from an enhanced greenhouse effect.
**National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** targets PM reduction.
**Methane** has a far higher warming potential than CO₂ per unit.
Global warming → sea-level rise, extreme weather, glacial melt.

glossary.definition: The Air Quality Index reporting daily air-pollution levels.
Warming from atmospheric gases trapping outgoing heat.
Biochemical Oxygen Demand — a measure of organic water pollution.

sections.heading: National action plans on climate change & disaster management

blocks.text: India tackles climate and disaster risk through the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC, 2008)** with its eight missions, and a **disaster-management framework** under the **DM Act (2005) and NDMA** aligned with the global Sendai Framework.

rows: **8 national missions** — Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge.
**SAPCC** — state action plans on climate change.

sections.heading: 🌿 Exam-ready deep coverage: NAPCC & disaster management

items: **NAPCC (2008) — 8 missions**: **National Solar Mission, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Sustaining Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change**; plus **State Action Plans (SAPCCs)**.
**Disaster management**: **Disaster Management Act 2005** → **NDMA (PM-chaired), SDMA, DDMA; NDRF** (response force); the shift from relief-centric to **prevention/mitigation/preparedness**.
**Frameworks**: **Sendai Framework 2015-30** (India a signatory); early-warning (IMD cyclones, INCOIS tsunami, CWC floods); **CDRI** (Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, India-led).
**AP relevance**: cyclone-prone coast → cyclone shelters, early warning, APSDMA.

prelimsPointers: **NAPCC (2008)** has **8 national missions** (Solar, Energy Efficiency, Water, Green India, Himalayan, Sustainable Habitat/Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge).
States prepare **SAPCC (State Action Plans on Climate Change)**.
